posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Throughout my 20 something years in investing, SpaceX $SPCX is the largest arbitrage I’ve ever encountered. It’s not a misunderstanding in the usual sense — it’s a cognitive error at market scale, and that error is the edge for anyone willing to look. 

Management has published guidance and data in the open; the spoon is right there in front of everyone. Yet large parts of the market still can’t see it, or simply refuse to, because the numbers are genuinely that extreme. I don’t know whether this window stays open for one year, two, or ten. But I suspect that whenever it closes, looking back will be one of the more interesting exercises in modern market history.

quote.author: cb_doge
quote.name: DogeDesigner
quote.text:
When @Starlink became a lifeline for a mother and her baby in rural Colombia.

Karina, 24, was facing a high-risk pregnancy after previously losing a baby. Reaching town from her remote community could take two days on horseback.

A visiting doctor brought a portable Starlink terminal and an ultrasound machine. Through Starlink, a specialist hundreds of kilometres away watched the scan live, guided the examination and identified the need for an immediate hospital transfer.

Karina reached the hospital in time. Her baby was born safely, and she had no complications.

Starlink brought specialist medical guidance into a home far from the city and helped a mother get urgent care.

This is why Starlink matters. It connects people to help when lives are at stake.

This lifesaving technology should be available in every part of the world.

posts.text:
I JUST GAVE GROK BOT A VOICE MAIL AND TEXT MESSAGING!

AND YOU CAN TOO—ITS FREE!

Your phone number is a front door. Most people leave it unlocked and unattended.

Meet Grok Bot Text & Voicemail, a front desk for your phone number that never takes a lunch break.

GET IT: https://x.ai/bot/z2ds5I1IWLO2M1lFFvhQ4

Think of it as a receptionist sitting between the world and your pocket. 

Texts and voicemails come in to a separate Google Voice number (this is until Grok Bot gets his own number from SpaceXSI).

It reads each one, figures out what the person wants and how urgent it is, and hands you a short note: "Joe’ Hair appointment wants to reschedule, medium urgency, here's a reply ready to go." You tap yes and it goes out as a text from your business number.

It works like a mail sorter for your attention. Real customers go to the top of the pile, spam goes in the trash, and urgent messages get flagged right away.

Where it shines:

Barbers and salons: "Got anything Thursday?" gets back three open slots from your calendar.

Contractors: It turns a rambling voicemail from a job site into one line: "Leak under kitchen sink, wants a quote, call back today."

Realtors: It sorts showing requests from people who are just curious.

Restaurants and food trucks: Hours, location, and catering questions get a reply ready in seconds.

Therapists and coaches: Clients book appointments without ever getting your personal cell.

Landlords: A maintenance emergency gets flagged as urgent, and "is it still available?" gets a draft reply.

Tutors, trainers, and photographers: Bookings land on a calendar just for the bot, and nothing gets double-booked.

Anyone selling on Marketplace or meeting people from dating apps: Hand out the bot's number, not yours.

It books appointments too. It reads your calendar, offers only real openings that fit your rules, and puts confirmed bookings on a calendar of their own.

You stay in charge. 

Every reply waits for your OK. 

Texts are capped to keep your number in good standing. You can raise the cap.

It's a seatbelt, not a megaphone. 

It's built to handle incoming messages well, not to blast texts out.

But wait, there's more!

It doesn't just answer your texts. It books appointments on your calendar.

Someone texts "Can I come in Thursday?" and in the old days that meant a game of phone tag: you check your calendar, text back, wait, they can't make it, and you check again.

Now it's like having a scheduler who already knows your whole week. 

The bot looks privately at every calendar you have, including work, family, and the kids' practices, and offers only times that are actually open. It follows your rules, too: your hours, how long appointments run, and the breathing room you want between them. Your family dinners won't get booked over, and neither will your lunch.

Bookings land on a calendar just for the bot, color-coded and kept separate from your other events, so you can see at a glance what your front desk booked.

Want the final say? Approve each booking with one tap. Ready to let it fly? Turn on auto-confirm and appointments book themselves while you work.

Haircuts: "Thursday at 2:15 works, see you then!" ✂️
Lessons: "Booked you for Tuesday at 3:40." 🎸
Estimates: "You're on for Friday at 1:20, address noted." 🔧
No booking apps, no back-and-forth, no double-booking. Just text in and appointment booked.
Your calendar finally answers the phone. 📅

Coming soon: outbound calls, and real Grok Bot phone numbers that will replace the Google Voice stand-in.
Your number is the front door. Put someone at the desk.

GET IT: https://x.ai/bot/z2ds5I1IWLO2M1lFFvhQ4
